# OpenAC / decomp comparison — round 5 findings ledger (2026-10-08)

Round 5 ran as one workflow (4 compare agents, one per area, and up to 4 adversarial verifiers, all read-only). Every finding
came back confirmed; the orchestrator re-read the load-bearing decomp citations (CharGenState::UpdateRemainingSkillCredits /
ResetSkillLevels / ApplyTemplate / SetSkillLevel, ACCharGenData::FormatName, ACCharGenResult::CG_Pack, the
VerifyCharacterGenerationResult skill rules, ItemUses::IsUseable / IsUseable_Targeted, ItemHolder::UseObject's altar branch,
HandleFailureEvent's PK cases, DoPKLite / DoPKArena / DoPKLArena, gmVendorUI::InqListSlotCount and Buy All, CM_Vendor::Event_Buy)
and implemented every finding except extcontainer-5, with the Rust compiled by the orchestrator only. Evidence per finding:

## Area summaries

### chargen

I compared holtburger's chargen code with retail and OpenAC. On the holtburger side that was holtburger-core CharacterGenBuilder, the holtburger-content catalog, the protocol pack/unpack, the plugins/character-creation.js wizard and the wasm sendCharGenResult/catalog exports. On the retail side it was the decomp (CharGenState, ACCharGenData, gmCGSkillsPage, gmCharGenMainUI, ACCharGenResult::CG_Pack/CG_UnPack and VerifyCharacterGenerationResult) plus OpenAC's CharGen/RuntimeCharacterCreationState. I also read the real CharGen record (0x0E000002) out of ~/ac_base_dats/client_portal.dat with a read-only script, and the baked data/skill-table.json. In the real data every heritage has 330 attribute and 52 skill credits, the only heritage skill override is Arcane Lore (0, 2), and all six preset templates cost exactly 52 under retail rules. The 0xF656 field order, the string alignment and the 0xF643 parse match retail, except that the trailing checksum is missing. The rule layer has two HIGH bugs that make the wizard broken against real data. First, specialising is charged trained + specialised (War Magic 44 instead of 28), so every preset template is over budget and the default flow cannot pass the Skills page. Second, every non-template skill is sent as Inactive, so the free skills (Run, Jump, Magic Defense, Loyalty, Salvaging, Arcane Lore) are never trained; a retail server would reject the packet. Smaller issues: clothing colours go out as list indices where retail sends palette-template keys; the retail name formatter is not applied; and unspent attribute credits are refused although retail allows them after a warning. One LOW item is not in the list below: 0xF643 rejections are shown as raw enum names. Retail maps them to ID_Character_Err_* text (likely 'The name you have selected is already in use.', 'Sorry, but that name is not permitted. Please choose another.', 'You do not have the privileges to make an administrator character.', and otherwise 'The server cannot create your new character at this time. Please try again later.'). An unknown code also makes the unpack fail, which leaves the wizard stuck in Submitting.

### containers

I compared holtburger's external-container window with the retail decomp and with OpenAC. On the holtburger side that is plugins/corpse-loot-bar.js, which container-panel.js routes every kind=21 to, the wasm ViewContents/CloseGroundContainer/groundContainerId code, item_drag/inventory_helpers drops and the picking.js use path. On the retail side it is gmExternalContainerUI, ClientUISystem::SetGroundObject/OnViewContents, ItemHolder::AttemptSetGroundObject/AttemptPlaceIn3D and CPlayerSystem::UsingItem plus the object-range handler. On the OpenAC side it is ExternalContainerState, ExternalContainerController and the lifecycle controller, plus their tests. Holtburger already has retail's one-window model and the shipped use-3/death-5/items-2 pieces. The gaps are in when the window opens and closes. (1) Every ViewContents opens or replaces the window, including the sub-packs ACE sends right after a chest/corpse opens and the player's own packs (pickup, vendor purchase, quest reward). The 1 s despawn poll then closes it, so any container holding a pack can't be looted. Retail opens only the requested ground object. (2) There is no client range exit, teleport/death close or vendor exclusivity. The window lingers up to ACE's 5 s heartbeat, or until the ~25 s prune after a portal, and a Take in that time walks the player back. (3) A 3D drop onto a container that isn't open drops the item on the ground; retail refuses it. (4) A locked chest gives no text. (5) Packs inside a chest can't be browsed. Not findings: holtburger closing with NoLongerViewingContents where retail/OpenAC send a toggle Use is the safer choice with ACE, because a Use that lands after ACE's own close re-opens the chest and walks the player back (Player_Use.cs:197). The blanket corpse drop refusal matches ACE ('container is Corpse' is refused, Player_Inventory.cs:853-857).

### vendorbuy

I compared holtburger-web's vendor BUY path against OpenAC and the retail decomp, and checked server behaviour against ACE's Vendor.cs and Player_Commerce.cs. The holtburger side covered vendor-ui.js, commerce_logic.js, the wasm VendorInfo cache (game_event.rs and lib.rs VendorStateJs), the 0xA0 arm and BuyActionData. The OpenAC side covered VendorUiController, VendorStagingList, VendorApproach, VendorRequests, VendorShopItemMaterializer, VendorSplitPolicy and their tests. The decomp side covered gmVendorUI::BuySingleItem, HandleButtonClicks, OpenVendor, InqListSlotCount and AdoptAsContents; VendorItemsUI::UpdateItemsList, AddToBuyList, RemoveFromShop and OpenVendor; VendorBuyUI::UpdateTransactionValue; ItemProfile::UnPack; CM_Vendor::Event_Buy; and ACCWeenieObject::ServerSaysAttemptFailed. Several parts are already correct: the single-stack ShopSystem::SellPrice math, the direction of the two rates, the trade-note rate, the alt-currency balance and the 2026-10-07 range close.

The gaps are in the flow around the formula:
1. Nothing is refused before sending. Retail refuses with "You don't have enough money" or "You must empty some slots in your backpack first", and a refused Buy All currently loses the whole list.
2. ACE's purchase refusal is shown as "You can't wield that!" plus a "WeenieError 0x0000" toast.
3. A stock line is priced as one lump and is not limited by its supply or by retail's 5000 cap, because the wasm drops ItemProfile.amount and max_stack_size.
4. A same-vendor refresh leaves stale entries on the buying list.
5. The category filter mislabels four item-type bits.
6. The Buy message lacks retail's trailing AlternateCurrencyId, and every VendorInfo adds a non-retail line to the Trade chat category.

Not reported because they are lower value or large:
- The close button has no confirmation ("You have not completed all transactions. Are you sure you want to leave this vendor?", HandleButtonClicks case 0x100000D6).
- Retail's starting quantity is the full stack except for 0x0DC41CB0 types, and its cost texts are not copied.
- Handle_VendorInfo's SetGroundObject(0,1): in retail, opening a vendor closes an open corpse or chest.
- @fillcomps (gmVendorUI::FillComponentList) is missing.
- "You can't wield that!" is used for every code-0 0xA0 on items, where retail builds the text from the outstanding request type.

ACE never resells stackables (Vendor.cs:631), so ACE's unique stock is always single non-stackable items and no whole-stack overcharge exists today.

### pkrules

I compared holtburger-web's PK handling with the retail decomp, using OpenAC as the worked reference. On the holtburger side I read objectIsAttackable and its callers in picking.js, entities.js and target_cycle.js, the spell target pre-check, the examine header, the character panel, the world-use paths, the slash-command router and the WeenieError text table. On the retail side I read ObjectIsAttackable, ExecuteAttack/GetAttackTarget/AutoTarget, the PK-status bit update (stat 0x86), ObjectCompatibleWithSpellTargetType/CastSpell, ItemHolder::UseObject and the PK/NPK altar dialogs, HandleFailureEvent, DoPKLite/DoPKArena/DoPKLArena, CharExamineUI and gmStatManagementUI::UpdatePKStatus. Several things already match retail: the attack rule itself, the spell pre-check (it reads live flags and the pet owner; retail does no PK check on spells), radar and bracket PK colours, the player-vs-player collision pass-through, and the PK jump-stamina rule. The main bug is that the melee/missile attack gate, Tab and auto-target, combat-mode entry and target tracking all read PK bits saved when the object was created. After any mid-session PK change (altar, @pklite, PK death and respite), a player who has just become PK cannot attack other PKs until they relog. The same stale data has no pet owner, so pets count as attack targets. Smaller gaps: using a PK or NPK altar skips retail's confirmation dialog; @pklite/@pkl, @pkarena/@pka and @pklarena/@pla are missing, so a player cannot enter PK Lite at all; the PK status and PK refusal messages print as garbled fallbacks (for example "You are now p k lite.") or reworded text; and the examine and character panels never show "Player Killer Lite" or "Non-Player Killer".
